doc.title: John Lamb interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 16, 2001

title: Ellington and Strayhorn collaborating; playing what you hear
summary: He saw Duke and Strayhorn work at the piano and was often given no bass parts.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: Yeah. Did you get to witness Duke collaborating with Strayhorn much?

Yeah. I’ve seen him come in and collaborate, preparing for a television show. They would talk around the piano. And I’ve seen them talk during recording sessions. Once Billy gave me some music and it was just measures and no notes. No chord changes. “Oh just play what you hear.” Yeah. Play what you hear. I’ve seen that. A lot of times they didn’t write anything for the bass.
That seems amazing to me. Because I mean that’s where it all starts.
And if you’re doing something that, well it certainly can change the sound of the whole thing.
Exactly. Maybe that was his trust that was coming through. Well I mean the band, you know, I have to prove that I’m worthy of being here I guess. So having that bass ear I was able to do that.
